## 2026-07-25T02:00:00Z voices protocol amendment — narrator as participant (the reported-speech voice attribution rollout)

- run_id: manual_voices_protocol_narrator_repeat_2026-07-25
- authorization: operator ruling on 2026-07-25, taken as a protocol amendment rather than an executor's judgment call. The question was open: neither docs/voices-protocol.md, docs/voices-protocol.md, AGENTS.md, nor any wiki/review/ note said where a narrator who also participates sits in voice_chain
- ruling: an utterance the narrator reports of themselves is a record one level BELOW the narration that reports it, owned by the narrator. Its chain therefore ends on an adjacent repeat (`["ΣΩ.", "ΣΩ."]`)
- bounds, both enforced by packages/harness/src/wiki/voices-validator.ts: repeats are permitted only in ONE ADJACENT pair (`chain_repeats_siglum` still rejects `["ΣΩ.", "ΚΛΕΙΝ.", "ΣΩ."]` and `["ΣΩ.", "ΣΩ.", "ΣΩ."]`); and a resolved record whose own owner is the repeat must cite a `person_marked_reporting_formula` with `role: cue` printed INSIDE its span, or it is the new `chain_repeat_unlicensed`. With no first-person formula in the span the utterance stays `unresolved`, never the narrator's by default
- rejected alternatives, recorded in the protocol: leaving these utterances at the narration level with no record (the enclosing record already spans the whole turn, so a verified narrator utterance and an unexamined stretch would compile to the same owner by inheritance — the defect this lane exists to remove); and registering a second siglum for the narrator-as-character (splits one person into two owners in claim.speaker, and the Greek prints ἐγώ, not a new name)
- why it could not stay open: rule 4 made the resolved form unwritable, which is why both wave-2 builders resolved zero spans to the narrator. `ἦν δ' ἐγώ` occurs 66 times in euthydemus and 43 in protagoras, and migration is all-or-nothing, so the wave-2 cutover could not have succeeded for either dialogue
- Symposium precedent, checked not assumed: the ratified ledger already places narrator-as-participant spans one level down — 23 unresolved depth-4 records with chain ΑΠΟΛ. → ΑΡΙΣΤΟΔ. → ΣΩ. inside the Diotima conversation. They stay correct and byte-unchanged under this amendment: Plato writes those replies bare (`μάλιστά γε.`), with no formula to cite
- code review discharged in the same commit: the two changes docs/voices-protocol.md §6 flagged were re-derived from the code. Both stand; each had one real defect, both fixed here. PUB-CI resolved the CI contract by matching a `.ts` token, so an inline-chained `bun run ci` script failed a correct setup — the contract is now checked wherever the manifest resolves it, and the `/process\.exit\(1\)/` proxy's limits are documented in the code. validSpeakers unioned the pre-registered voice-sigla SUPERSET into the allowed set for dialogues with no authoritative voice index, where owner-equality is not enforced either, so a hand-edited `speaker: "ΠΡΟΔ."` in protagoras passed on a siglum no record licenses; the union is now gated on the dialogue having an authoritative index
- disposition: wiki/review/2026-07-25-symposium-voice-cutover-execution.md is ACCEPTED on the basis of that review, so the reported-speech voice attribution rollout's wave-2 gate is satisfied
- review_statuses: none changed. No record in any lane changed status, and no claim speaker moved
- authority boundary: docs, validator, and tests only. No Greek source, turn index, observation, claim, relation, commentary, or voice record modified; no voice index or join derived
- review note: wiki/review/2026-07-25-symposium-cutover-code-review.md

## 2026-07-30T01:45:00Z Symposium registry ruling four, and the role_reporting_formula case amendment

- run_id: manual_reported_turn_completion_pais_and_role_formula_2026-07-29
- authorization: operator ruling 2026-07-29, the Symposium re-review. The same session's earlier ruling registered ΓΛΑΥ., ΖΕΥΣ. and ΗΦΑΙ. at `eadc5a7` and carried no ingest-log entry, being registry-only; this entry covers the fourth owner and, because it is a contract change, the schema amendment that owner forced
- registry: `ΠΑΙΣ.` added to the Symposium block of `derived/plato/voices/sigla.toml`. It denotes **the one announcing servant of 175a**, owner of the `{q}`-marked first-person direct speech at `[5990, 6097)` (`κἀμοῦ καλοῦντος οὐκ ἐθέλει εἰσιέναι`), transmitted by `ἄλλον δέ τινα τῶν παίδων ἥκειν ἀγγέλλοντα ὅτι` at `[5944, 5989)`. It does **not** denote servants collectively: the vocative plural `παῖδες` (175a, 213b) addresses the household staff as a group and licenses nothing, since a collective addressee is not an owner
- why it was blocked: both blind reviews of the 74 legacy unresolved records independently reached BLOCKED-ON-REGISTRY for `voice_symposium_0006` and neither invented a siglum. The record could be expressed neither as resolved (no id for its owner) nor as honestly unresolved (only one possible owner, so no set of two registered candidates exists). The failure was about the registry, not about the Greek
- form note: `ΠΑΙ.` is a printed turn siglum in `laches.txt` and `meno.txt` for a different person (Meno's slave boy). `ΠΑΙΣ.` deliberately takes a distinct form so no record implies the two are the same speaker
- schema: amended evidence kind `role_reporting_formula` in `docs/voices-protocol.md`. It required a definite role description as **nominative** subject, which no construction at 175a satisfies — narrated dialogue puts the reporting construction into accusative-and-infinitive, where the subject of the report is accusative by grammatical necessity. The test is now the **syntactic role, not the case**: the role-denoting phrase must be the grammatical subject of the reporting construction, nominative of a finite verb or accusative of a reporting infinitive/participle
- what the amendment does not do: an accusative that is the *object* of the governing verb is still not a subject. The trap is recorded in the protocol — at Symposium 213b (char 84958) `μεταστρεφόμενον αὐτὸν ὁρᾶν τὸν Σωκράτη, ἰδόντα δὲ … εἰπεῖν`, `τὸν Σωκράτη` is the object of `ὁρᾶν` and the utterance is Alcibiades's. A matcher keying on "reporting verb near a named accusative" attributes it to the wrong speaker
- also unchanged: the kind stays separate from `named_reporting_formula`, because the source prints no proper name and an oblique subject does not change that. An indefinite introduction (`τινα`) does not disqualify a phrase that denotes one specific individual, but a genuine plural or collective is not a reported turn at all
- registration authorizes nothing further: per the superset contract an entry earns no attribution, and `voice_symposium_0006` still needs its own licensing evidence on the record. The amendment widens which constructions the kind can cite; it changes no existing record and decides no attribution
- review_statuses: none changed. No voice record, claim, observation, relation, commentary record or audio artifact was modified; no cohort extracted; no index or join recompiled; no claim speaker moved
